claude.sample_unit: ICU admissions (14,294 development in MIMIC-IV; 21,677 external in eICU-CRD)

links.outcome: Calibration after out-of-sample logistic recalibration following prevalence shift
links.effect: Calibration shifted with event prevalence (over-prediction in temporal split, under-prediction in external cohort); a single logistic recalibration largely corrected the shift in both directions.
links.quote: a single logistic recalibration largely corrected the shift in both directions.

links.outcome: Discrimination on temporal and external geographic validation without refitting
links.effect: Gradient-boosting AUROC 0.764 internal CV, 0.733 temporal validation, 0.767 external validation in eICU-CRD; discrimination moderate and stable, calibration shifted.
links.quote: Discrimination was moderate and stable across all settings (gradient-boosting area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve 0.764 [95% CI 0.755–0.773] for internal cross-validation, 0.733 [0.710–0.754] for temporal validation, and 0.767 [0.760–0.774] for external validation).

links.effect: Calibration over-predicted when temporal prevalence fell and under-predicted when external prevalence rose.
links.quote: In contrast, calibration shifted predictably with event prevalence — over-prediction when prevalence fell across the temporal split and under-prediction when it rose in the external cohort — while the calibration slope remained close to, or slightly below, one; a single logistic recalibration largely corrected the shift in both directions.

links.effect: Gradient-boosting and ridge models performed similarly.
links.quote: The gradient-boosting and ridge models performed similarly.

links.effect: Portable discrimination but prevalence-dependent calibration across time and populations.
links.quote: A model predicting haemodynamic intolerance at the de-resuscitation decision showed portable discrimination but prevalence-dependent calibration that was largely correctable by simple recalibration.

links.effect: A single logistic recalibration largely corrected over-prediction temporally and under-prediction externally.
